subject: SLA litmus: transient checkout interruptions — entitlement & evidence request
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@meridianpay.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ops+billing@meridianpay.com
Date: Tue, 26 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Checkout interruptions on 2028-06-25 — confirmation & credits

Markus / Laura,

We saw a spike of failed checkouts for several of our merchants last night starting roughly 22:48 UTC and resolving around 23:05 UTC (Meridian internal timestamps attached). The failures correlated with 500/503 responses for tokenization and a small burst of retry storms in our sidecar. We need Redwood to confirm whether this window aligns with any backend outage or degraded availability on your side, and whether this qualifies for SLA credit under our agreement.

Specific asks:
- Can you confirm the service availability window on Redwood for region us-west-2 between 2028-06-25T22:45Z and 2028-06-25T23:10Z?
- If eligible, what is the proposed credit calculation and timeframe to issue it?
- Please share the postmortem invite and a short timeline of next steps — our ops and billing teams both need to be looped.

I've attached our local trace samples and a CSV of affected checkout IDs.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Integrations, MeridianPay

- Initial signal: elevated 5xx rate from tokenization endpoint across a subset of instances in usw2; coincident autoscaler activity shows a brief failure to add pods during a scaledown window.
- Hypothesis: warmup delay + cold-starts for a new model variant coupled with prefix-cache evictions may have increased tail latency, triggering client retries that amplified load.

Immediate asks:
- Diego: pull runtime traces (KV cache evictions, prefetch logs) for 22:30–23:20 UTC and supply the trace bundle to Markus. Prioritize instances tagged cluster-usw2-prod-a.
- Hannah: extract autoscaler events and instance lifecycle logs for the same window; check for any API errors returned by the control plane during scale operations.
- Laura: prepare the SLA eligibility worksheet (monthly availability baseline, impacted tokens/requests) and a draft credit calc (pro rata) — use DEAL-87421 terms.

Keep comms internal until we validate the exact window; we'll send a consolidated response to MeridianPay once we have the logs and the proposed calc.

Samir — thank you again for the samples and patience. We completed a preliminary investigation and here is our current position: 

Confirmed timeline: 2028-06-25 22:47:30Z – 2028-06-25 23:04:58Z (17 minutes, 28 seconds) saw elevated 5xx responses and increased tail latency for the tokenization path in us-west-2. The attached runtime_traces_20280625_2248-2305.zip contains the raw spans and instance logs we used to validate.

Root cause (short): an autoscaler scale-out race coupled with a model-variant warmup regression. During a scheduled scaledown window an older autoscaler snapshot prevented expected capacity from coming online fast enough; newly launched instances experienced longer-than-expected kernel warmup, producing elevated error rates and missed keepalives. Retries from client SDKs amplified the pressure.

SLA eligibility and proposed credit: per the DEAL-87421 SLA terms, this window reduces available uptime for the calendar month below the 99.9% threshold for affected tenant weight. We propose a prorated credit equal to 0.6% of MeridianPay's monthly committed spend for June 2028. The proposed_credit_calc.xlsx attached shows the math and the billable period.

Next steps: 
- If MeridianPay agrees, we can apply the credit to your next invoice. Please reply with confirmation or a counter proposal. Alternatively we can issue a one-time invoice adjustment; let us know the preference.
- We're scheduling a postmortem for 2028-06-29 15:00 PT (calendar invite link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBCf-postmortem-invite). The postmortem will include engineering, reliability, and your integrations team to cover mitigation steps and rollout hardening.
- We will patch the warmup path and adjust autoscaler snapshot tests; a targeted rollout is planned for 2028-07-03.

Attachments included: runtime_traces_20280625_2248-2305.zip, request_sample_merchant-checkout-ids.csv, proposed_credit_calc.xlsx

Sorry for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority. Please let us know how you'd like the credit delivered and if you want the postmortem time adjusted.

Best,
